page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is network-based with a local capacity of 1 GB, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals highly polarized performance characteristics. The server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3688.67 and exceptional single-threaded compression and decompression speeds, with gzip compression reaching 39.96 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.65 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics are significantly weaker. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU score both fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory read bandwidth is also limited, though write bandwidth for large blocks remains average at 28.99 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-threaded capabilities, this instance is suited for workloads that do not require heavy parallelization or high memory throughput. It achieves average performance in static web serving at 8.04 GB/sec and small-model LLM text generation at 106.45 tokens/sec. However, it is poorly suited for database operations, with PassMark database benchmarks scoring in the bottom 10% and Redis SET operations performing in the bottom 25%. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and simple utility tasks, while resource-dense databases or multi-threaded processing should be avoided.

It is configured with 8.0 GB of RAM, 1 GB of network-based local storage, and no GPU. Performance benchmarks show a stark contrast: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression rank in the top tier, whereas multi-core performance, memory read bandwidth, and database operations fall into the lower percentiles. This hardware profile offers dedicated compute resources at an entry-level scale, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that rely on single-threaded speed rather than parallel processing. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded utility scripts, and basic application hosting, while complex database systems and multi-threaded workloads are limited by its memory and multi-core constraints.
